tagline.text: A fairy's legend held in sapphire waters of unknown depth

items.credit: Bro. Jeffrey  Pioquinto, SJ from Dublin, Ireland, Philippines / CC BY 2.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A short river flowing through the forest at Hinatuan on Mindanao's east coast, where water welling up from a deep underwater cave takes on a striking sapphire and clear turquoise hue. Famous for its legend of resident fairies and the sight of fish schools surfacing at the midday feeding, it's a signature attraction of Surigao del Sur.

Enchanted River (Hinatuan Enchanted River) flows through the forest of Talisay village in Hinatuan, on Mindanao's eastern Pacific coast, in Surigao del Sur Province. The river itself isn't long and soon empties into Hinatuan Bay, but its deep upstream pool shows an overlapping cobalt blue and clear turquoise so vivid that photos of it look color-corrected. Travelers seeing it for the first time often say it looks "like paint spilled into water."

This mysterious color comes from the river's structure. At the bottom of its deepest pool lies an underwater cave connected to the limestone bedrock below, from which clear water constantly wells up. The water is so clear and deep that sunlight can't reach the bottom in places, making those areas appear a deep blue. The pool is said to be over
deep, though how far the cave extends is not yet fully known, and it's notable for being close enough to the sea that fresh and salt water mix.

Local legend tells of fairies (encanto) living in this river. A common tale says the large fish in the river can never be caught no matter how you fish, and that at night the fairies swim and sing in the water. This legend combined with the surreal water color gave rise to the name "Enchanted River."
For a long time it was a secret spot known only to locals, but after photos spread online in the late

, travelers began flocking here from across the Philippines. Today, Hinatuan city manages visitors, setting designated swimming areas and hours. Though it's far to reach, it's a must-visit for travelers planning a Surigao del Sur trip alongside nearby Tinuy-an Falls and the Britania Islands.
You can enter the water within the designated area wearing a life vest. The water is a bit cooler than the sea and extremely clear, letting you see schools of fish right beneath your feet.
Around midday (and sometimes around
3 PM
depending on the day), when the caretaker scatters feed, large and small fish rise all at once from the depths. Swimming pauses briefly during this time, so watch from the water's edge.

blocks.title: Photographing the river view from the wooden bridge

children.text: Looking down from the bridge and steps crossing the river, you can see the full gradation from turquoise to deep navy at a glance. It's most vivid in the strong midday sun.
Walking downstream from the pool, the river widens and mangroves and forest continue along it. With fewer people around, it's a good spot to quietly enjoy the water.

blocks.title: Touring the lower river by bangka

children.text: When operating, a small boat lets you go down to where the river meets the sea. The color shift where fresh and salt water mix is striking.
Talking with the caretaker and locals about legends like the uncatchable fish or the singing heard at night makes the river feel even more mysterious.
Rental huts along the riverbank are a good place to eat food you've brought and rest. It's a nice way to pass the time between swimming and the feeding show.

The most efficient itinerary is swimming and watching the feeding at Enchanted River in the morning, then moving to Tinuy-an Falls in the afternoon for a bamboo raft ride, before staying overnight in Bislig.

Surigao del Sur, facing the Pacific on Mindanao's east coast, gets heavy rain year-round. From
November
to
February
especially, the northeast monsoon brings frequent downpours that can cloud the water and cause landslides that block roads. Visiting during the relatively dry period from
March
to
September
gives the best chance of the clearest, most vivid water color.
Water color also varies by time of day even on the same day. Between
10 AM and 1 PM
, when the sun is highest, sunlight penetrates deepest and the contrast between turquoise and navy is most striking. On weekends, holidays, and during summer break (April–
May
), local visitors increase sharply and the swimming area gets crowded, so weekday mornings are recommended. The water can turn cloudy the day after heavy rain.

Lodging around Enchanted River is limited. Downtown Hinatuan and the nearby coast have a few small resorts and guesthouses (about
per night), and for more options, staying in Bislig (Mangagoy), about
1 hour
away, is a good choice. Bislig has several hotels at about
per night, making it convenient for combining with Tinuy-an Falls.

There are small stalls by the river selling simple drinks, snacks, and rice meals, but the options are limited. If possible, it's better to buy grilled chicken, fish, or fruit at the Hinatuan market and eat it at a cottage. The Surigao del Sur coast has fresh, cheap seafood — crab, shrimp, and shellfish — and coconut-milk ginataan and vinegar-cured kinilaw are common local dishes.
Hinatuan and Bislig have few ATMs, and the riverside accepts cash only, so withdraw enough in Butuan or Davao.
Since swimming pauses during the fish feeding, it's efficient to plan swimming for early morning and viewing for around noon.
A polarizing (CPL) filter reduces surface glare for much more vivid water colors in photos; with a phone, angle it slightly off the water's surface when shooting.
The river water is colder than it looks, so a rash guard or thin wetsuit lets you swim longer.
Cell signal is weak, so arrange your habal-habal driver's contact and return time in advance.
A waterproof bag, towel, change of clothes, and slippers make moving around after swimming easier.
Enchanted River and Tinuy-an Falls can be combined in one day, but adding the Britania Islands requires 2 nights in Bislig.
The river has sections deeper than
leading into an underwater cave. Do not swim outside the designated area or enter without a life vest, and scuba or freediving is prohibited without local government permit.
Swimming hours, visitor limits, and entrance fees change frequently under Hinatuan city regulations, so check the latest notices before visiting.
Throwing snacks or bread to the fish, or trying to catch them, is prohibited. Only the caretaker may feed them.
To protect the water quality, don't apply excessive sunscreen or lotion before entering, and shampoo or soap use is not allowed.
During the rainy season, landslides and road flooding can delay buses, so allow extra travel time.
Some parts of Mindanao carry travel advisories, so check your foreign ministry's travel safety information beforehand and avoid late-night long-distance travel.
